implementationHash.description: Digest of what the scorer actually does — the canonicalized predicate, or the judge prompt plus template version. Required so two judges with different prompts cannot hash identically.

label.description: Presentation only; deliberately excluded from the hash.

role.description: Only `gating` scorers decide the iteration's verdict.

onError.description: What an `error` status does to a gating iteration. Defaults to `fail`.

onSkipped.description: What a `skipped` status does to a gating iteration. Separate from `onError`: a crashed judge and a judge that never ran are different failures.

EvaluationConfigSnapshot.description: The scorer definitions a run graded with, plus their hash. Changing scorer configuration changes this hash but NOT the case identity — a threshold edit must not fork a scenario's history.

hash.description: `evaluationConfigHash` over the resolved definitions. Order-independent — the hash sorts internally.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Omitted on the last page.

serverUrl.description: The MCP server URL the tokens were obtained for.

oauthResourceUrl.description: OAuth protected-resource URL, when it differs from `serverUrl`.

clientInformation.description: OAuth client used to obtain the tokens. Optional, but without it server-side refresh cannot run — always include it when you provide a `refresh_token`.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token expires.

id.description: Pass as `organizationId` to the project routes.

myRole.description: The caller's role in the organization.

isCreator.description: Whether the caller created the organization.

role.description: Caller's role on the project, when resolved.

ProjectServer.description: A saved MCP server, projected toward the hosted (HTTP) shape. STDIO command/args/env and raw headers are never exposed.

url.description: Endpoint for HTTP-transport servers; `null` for stdio.

passRateTrend.description: Recent runs' pass rates, oldest first.

EvalCheckRepo.description: A repository whose pull requests run an eval suite.

suiteId.description: The eval suite this repository's pull requests run.

outagePolicy.description: What the check reports when MCPJam cannot conclude. `null` is a REAL state — nobody chose a policy, because the repository was connected before the choice existed. The effective behaviour is `fail_open`, but reporting `fail_open` would say someone picked it.

available.description: Whether GitHub Checks is available for this organization at all. `false` and "available, nothing connected" are different situations, and only one of them is fixed by connecting a repository.

connectable.description: The repositories the MCPJam GitHub App can reach — the choices a connect has. `null` means the question could not be ASKED: the lookup itself failed (GitHub unreachable, or the call errored); the connected `items` still stand, as they need no GitHub call. An EMPTY list means it was asked and came back with nothing, which covers two situations the platform does not distinguish: the App is installed but reaches no repository, and this deployment has no App installation at all. If a connect is failing against an empty list, check the installation before assuming a permissions problem.

suiteId.description: The eval suite this repository's pull requests will run.

repo.description: `owner/repo`. Canonicalized and VERIFIED against the App's installation before it is stored.

outagePolicy.description: REQUIRED here, though the platform leaves it optional for a deploy window: a surface that defaults it is the one that quietly produces repositories nobody chose a policy for.

EvalSuiteComputerEnvironment.description: The sandbox image a suite's eval runs boot from.

name.description: The image's name, resolved for you so a caller can echo back what it set. `null` when the pinned image could not be resolved (deleted, or not visible to this caller).

EvalSuiteSchedule.description: Recurring-run schedule. A schedule fires exactly ONE run, so an environment-based suite pins the environment it runs against.

intervalMinutes.description: Minutes between runs. 5 minutes to 7 days.

environmentId.description: The single attached environment scheduled runs use. Null on a legacy (non-environment) suite.

EvalSuiteScheduleRequest.description: Enable, repoint, or disable a suite's recurring runs. Disabling PRESERVES the existing environment pin — send `enabled: true` with a new `environmentId` to repoint it.

environmentId.description: Which attached environment scheduled runs use. Only meaningful when enabling. Omitted on a single-environment suite means that environment; omitted on a multi-environment suite is a VALIDATION_ERROR.

EvalSuiteUpdateRequest.description: Partial update of a suite's settings. Omitted fields are left as they are.

computerEnvironment.description: Sandbox-image name or id. `null` clears the pin (runs fall back to the provider's default base image). Enumerate the choices with `list_sandbox_images`.

environmentIds.description: Tri-state: a non-empty array sets/replaces the attachments, `null` CLEARS them (reverting the suite to legacy config), and `[]` is REJECTED rather than silently read as a clear.

servers.description: Server names (as bound in the suite's environment) or project-server ids.

minimumIterations.description: Suite-level floor on per-case iterations: every case runs at least this many times (`max(case.iterations, minimumIterations)`). `null` clears it.

autoRun.description: The flag the grader actually gates on. Without it a suite can be `enabled` forever and never grade a run.

SessionLink.description: Where a human goes to read this session. Prefers the surface-native page; falls back to `/sessions?session=` when the session has none (an eval Quick Run, or a deleted parent run).

url.description: Absolute URL for the same target.

SessionParentRef.description: The session's parent run, discriminated on `kind`. Additive: switch on `kind` and tolerate an unknown value.

label.description: Human-readable parent name; null when the parent row is gone.

suiteRunId.description: eval only; null means Quick Run (no suite run exists).

chatSessionId.description: Wire id used by the Playground restore; distinct from `id`.

visibility.description: Direct sessions only: `private` or `project`. Null elsewhere.

cumulativeUserMessageCount.description: Absent (not 0) when the session never reported the counter.

matchPreview.description: `scope=transcripts` only: a window of the transcript around the match. Null when no window could be located; absent entirely on title-scope results.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. Omitted on the last page.

scope.description: The scope the server actually honored. ABSENT from deployments predating the parameter — treat its absence as "transcript search unsupported".

nextCursor.description: Pass as `before` to fetch the next page. Omitted on the last page.

expiresAt.description: Epoch milliseconds when the stored access token expires, or `null` if unknown.

ScenarioLink.description: Share link for the scenario. The URL embeds the access token; visible to any caller who can read the scenario (the same audience that sees it in the hosted UI).

ScenarioServer.description: A server attached to the scenario. Scenarios attach HTTP servers only, so `url` is the server's endpoint.

ProjectScenario.description: Summary of a published scenario, as returned by the list endpoint.

hostStyle.description: Chat surface style the scenario renders (e.g. `claude`, `chatgpt`).

hostId.description: The named host the scenario publishes (hosts and scenarios are 1:1).

ScenarioDetail.description: A scenario's full read-only settings: the summary fields plus the host execution config and resolved servers.

hostStyle.description: Chat surface style the scenario renders (e.g. `claude`, `chatgpt`).

hostId.description: The named host the scenario publishes (hosts and scenarios are 1:1).

name.description: Server name to register the tunnel under. Reusing an existing server's name points that record at the tunnel: its `url` is overwritten and stdio records are converted to `transportType: "http"`.

TunnelGrant.description: Everything the caller needs to host the tunnel connection. **Treat the whole object as a credential**: `url` embeds the plaintext `?k=` bearer secret and `connectToken` authenticates the relay WebSocket.

existed.description: True when a server record with this name already existed (its config now points at the tunnel).

previousUrl.description: The record's previous URL, present when it existed with a different one (it has been overwritten).

previousTransportType.description: The record's previous transport, present when it existed (a `stdio` record has been converted to `http`).

slug.description: Stable public subdomain slug; survives re-creates for the same server.

url.description: Public tunnel URL including the `?k=` bearer secret. Also persisted on the server record's `url`.

connectToken.description: Bearer for the relay edge WebSocket handshake.

relayWsUrl.description: Relay edge WebSocket endpoint to connect to.

secretVersion.description: Monotonic secret version; each create bumps it.

Client.description: A client in a project, as returned by the client list.

configId.description: ID of the content-addressed config this client points at. Content addressed, so the same id means byte-identical settings — send it back as `expectedConfigId` on a write to make the write compare-and-set.

serverCount.description: Number of MCP servers attached to the client config.

ownerScope.description: Product ownership of the row (null for untagged clients). Never an authorization signal.

hasComputer.description: Whether the live config attaches a computer.

ClientImpact.description: What a config edit to this client would follow. These are the DURABLE consumers that re-resolve the client's current config; past runs, per-turn traces and pinned eval-suite snapshots hold a config id and are unaffected. Direct playground and client-chat use follows the edit too and has no row to count.

liveEnvironmentCount.description: Non-archived project environments selecting this client.

scenarioAttachmentCount.description: Scenario attachments re-materialized inside the edit transaction.

activeLegacyJourneyCount.description: Active journeys with no environments that pin this client.

ClientDetail.description: A client plus its resolved config (model, capabilities, host context, MCP profile) and the read-backs an editor needs.

config.description: Client config v2 DTO. Opaque object; shape mirrors the inspector's client editor.

ClientCreateRequest.description: Create a client from a built-in template OR a full config. Exactly one of `template` or `config` is required.

name.description: Display name for the new client.

template.description: Built-in template id to seed the host config from.

theme.description: Theme stamped into the seeded config (template only).

modelId.description: Model id the client pins. Required and non-empty: an environment inherits its client's model when it sets no override, so a client created without one cannot back a headless environment and its launches are refused with `ENV_MODEL_REQUIRED`. A `PATCH` may not clear it either, though clients created before this rule stay editable.

config.description: Full client config v2, used verbatim (alternative to `template`). Must pin `modelId`.

ClientUpdateRequest.description: Edit a client. Provide at least one of `name`, `config` (whole-config replacement) or `set` (named fields); `config` and `set` are mutually exclusive. Config edits require `expectedConfigId` and renames require `expectedName`, so a concurrent edit is rejected rather than overwritten.

expectedName.description: The `name` you last read for this client. REQUIRED whenever the request sends `name`: a rename does not rotate the config, so `expectedConfigId` cannot detect a concurrent one. A mismatch is `409 CONFLICT` carrying `details.currentName`.

expectedConfigId.description: The `configId` you last read for this client. REQUIRED whenever the request changes the config (`config` or `set`): without it a write composed from a stale read silently reverts whatever landed in between. A mismatch is `409 CONFLICT` carrying `details.currentConfigId`.

expectedImpact.description: The `impact` you last read for this client. Optional, and checked transactionally when sent — a consumer added or removed since you read it makes the write conflict (`details.currentImpact`) instead of quietly affecting more than you were told it would.

config.description: Replacement client config v2. Replaces the config wholesale; use `set` to change named fields instead.

ClientFieldSet.description: Named fields to change, applied over the client's current config INSIDE the write transaction. Absent always means keep. `null` means "make it go away", and what that means depends on the field: a required field resets to its documented default, an optional one clears to absent. Object-valued fields are whole-object replacements, not merges — to change a deep knob, read the client, overlay the sub-object, and send it back whole. `hostStyle`, `clientCapabilities`, `hostContext` and server membership are deliberately not settable here (use a whole-`config` replacement, or the servers operation).

modelId.description: Model id the client pins. Value only — there is no `null`, and a blank string is refused: a client that pins a model cannot be edited into one that does not.

systemPrompt.description: Send `null` to reset this field to its canonical default. Default: `""`.

temperature.description: Send `null` to reset this field to its canonical default. Default: `0.7`.

requireToolApproval.description: Send `null` to reset this field to its canonical default. Default: `false`.

connectionDefaults.description: Send `null` to reset this field to its canonical default. Default: empty headers and the platform's default request timeout.

respectToolVisibility.description: Send `null` to clear this field back to absent.

progressiveToolDiscovery.description: Send `null` to clear this field back to absent.

harness.description: Execution runtime selector. Send `null` to clear this field back to absent. Setting one requires the matching feature flag; clearing never does.

computer.description: Send `null` to clear this field back to absent. Attaching one requires the computers feature flag; detaching never does.

builtInToolIds.description: Send `null` to clear this field back to absent.

skillSelection.description: `{ mode: "all-visible" }` or `{ mode: "explicit", skillIds: [...] }`. Send `null` to clear this field back to absent.

modelVisibleMcpToolResults.description: Send `null` to clear this field back to absent.

mcpToolResultImageRendering.description: Send `null` to clear this field back to absent.

mcpProfile.description: Send `null` to clear this field back to absent.

hostCapabilitiesOverride.description: Send `null` to clear this field back to absent.

chatUiOverride.description: Send `null` to clear this field back to absent.

SandboxImageBuild.description: One build of a sandbox image's image.

baseImageDigests.description: Resolved sha256 digest of every FROM base (the reproducibility pin).

logPreview.description: Capped, ANSI-stripped tail of the build log.

SandboxImage.description: A project's custom Computer image: a digest-pinned blueprint plus its latest build.

sharing.description: `user` = a personal draft; `project` = shared with the whole project.

blueprint.description: The image's blueprint YAML (base / initialize / maintenance / knowledge). `base` must be an allowlisted official image pinned by sha256 digest.

SandboxImageCreateRequest.description: Create a sandbox image from a blueprint YAML document: an allowlisted, `@sha256`-digest-pinned `base` image plus `initialize` steps baked into the image, and optional `maintenance`/`knowledge` delivered to the agent at runtime.

name.description: Display name for the new sandbox image; must be non-empty after trimming.

blueprint.description: Blueprint YAML defining the image. Validated server-side; use the validate endpoint for fast feedback.

SandboxImageUpdateRequest.description: Edit a sandbox image. Provide at least one of `name` or `blueprint`; only the fields you pass change.

name.description: New display name; must be non-empty after trimming.

blueprint.description: Replacement blueprint YAML. Edits to maintenance/knowledge take effect at the next chat turn without a rebuild; base/initialize edits require a new build.

SandboxImageBuildStarted.description: A build was accepted (202). It runs in the background — poll the builds list for status.

reused.description: True when an identical prior build was reused instead of rebuilding.

status.description: The computer's lifecycle status after attaching (it re-provisions).

EnvironmentSkillSelection.description: An explicit pinned skill selection. Cannot be empty — clear the field instead (send `null` on update) to mean "no pinned skills".

skillIds.description: Project-shared skill IDs. Plugin-component skills cannot be selected — they reach a run by pinning their plugin version.

versionPins.description: Optional exact-version overlay: at most one entry per selected skill, each naming a version of that same skill. A selected skill with no entry runs "Latest" — its current revision, resolved when the run starts. Pin a version to hold this environment at a known revision, e.g. to compare two revisions of one skill side by side.

EnvironmentSecretSelection.description:
Which PROJECT SECRETS a run launched from this environment receives — ids only. The environment is the GRANT BOUNDARY: absent means no secrets, and there is no "all of them" mode. Cannot be empty; clear the field instead (send `null` on update) to revoke the grant.

Membership is not delivery. A `sharing: user` secret selected here reaches ONLY sessions its owner started; every other member's run of this environment silently does not receive it, and that rule is re-checked live at launch rather than baked into the selection.

secretIds.description: Secret IDs, as returned by the project's secret list.

ProjectEnvironment.description: A project environment: a named, live-editable execution bundle that eval suites and journeys run against.

name.description: Unique among the project's live (non-archived) environments.

hostId.description: The host this environment runs against.

serverAttachmentId.description: Present only when the environment pins a standalone server group; otherwise the host config's own servers apply.

modelId.description: The environment's model override. ABSENT means the environment INHERITS the model pinned on its host — not that it has no model. Resolve the environment and read `effectiveModelId` to learn what will actually run.

pluginVersionIds.description: Pinned plugin VERSION IDs. Narrow by design: the plugin must be installed and enabled, the version must be `ready`, at most one version per plugin may be pinned, and none of its skills may carry supporting files. Not a general-purpose plugin list.

sandboxImageId.description: Sandbox-image pin: a project-shared image (see the images endpoints) that eval runs in this environment boot a fresh sandbox from. Absent when unpinned.

revision.description: Optimistic-concurrency counter. Pass this back as `expectedRevision` on the next write; if it no longer matches, the write is rejected with 409 instead of overwriting a concurrent edit.

archived.description: Archived environments cannot be edited or launched until restored.

archivedAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds. Present only when archived.

Plugin.description: An Agent Plugin (agent-plugins.org bundle) imported into a project. Versions materialize MCP servers and skills; environments pin version ids to run them.

name.description: Normalized plugin name — the namespace its skills load under.

enabled.description: Disabled plugins keep their versions but resolve for no run.

activeVersionId.description: The version environment pins default to. Absent before the first activation.

PluginVersion.description: One immutable imported plugin version with its component projections.

status.description: Only `ready` versions resolve at runtime.

componentCounts.description: Per-component tallies. `apps` counts preserved `.app.json` metadata entries only (no runtime effect).

servers.description: Declared MCP server components, with the project server row each one materialized as.

placement.description: Where the component can execute; `local`/`computer` components never run on MCPJam hosted servers.

skills.description: Declared skill components, with the project skill row each one materialized as.

name.description: Load-bearing identity: the on-box directory name and the `loadSkill` argument. Immutable — renames are rejected.

sharing.description: `project` skills are shared with the organization and are the only ones an environment may pin. `user` skills are the caller's own drafts.

aggregateHash.description: Drift key over the body and any supporting files. A skill body is mutable and an edit overwrites it in place, so this is the only handle on WHICH content a given pin resolved to.

provenance.description: How the row came to exist (`authored`, `computer-adopted`, …). Absent on older records; treat an unknown value as `authored`.

pinnability.description: Whether this skill may be pinned into an environment. ABSENT means unknown (an older backend), which is not the same as eligible.

reason.description: Why not, when `ok` is false — e.g. the skill is personal, carries supporting files, or carries extra frontmatter.

content.description: The SKILL.md body, with frontmatter stripped.

AdhocEnvironment.description: An UNNAMED, content-addressed environment: a composed client/model/computer/skills stack rather than a saved entry in the project's environment list. Its own shape rather than `ProjectEnvironment` with a nullable name, because that schema's `name` is required and every environment listing filters ad-hoc rows out precisely so that promise holds.

name.description: Always `null` — an ad-hoc environment is unnamed by construction.

adhoc.description: Always `true`. Present so a reader never has to infer it from the null name.

modelId.description: The stack's model override. Absent means it inherits the host's.

revision.description: Pass back as `expectedRevision` when promoting it with a name.

created.description: `false` when the same stack had already been composed. The only way to tell a first compose from a repeat — the status line cannot, because get-or-create answers `200` either way.

AdhocEnvironmentRequest.description: A composed stack: the same execution axes a named environment carries, minus the name.

hostId.description: The host the stack runs as.

serverAttachmentId.description: Standalone server group to pin. Omit to use the host's own servers.

modelId.description: Model to run instead of the host's pinned one. Stored verbatim.

pluginVersionIds.description: Pinning plugin versions requires project ADMIN; the rest of a stack needs only membership.

sandboxImageId.description: Project-shared sandbox image to pin, so runs boot a fresh computer from it.

expectedRevision.description: The revision you last read. Stale ⇒ `409`.

name.description: Must be unique among the project's live environments.

modelId.description: Model to run instead of the host's; omit to inherit the host's. Stored verbatim — no alias canonicalization — so pass exactly the id the provider request should carry.

pluginVersionIds.description: Pinned plugin VERSION IDs. Narrow by design: the plugin must be installed and enabled, the version must be `ready`, at most one version per plugin may be pinned, and none of its skills may carry supporting files. Not a general-purpose plugin list.

sandboxImageId.description: Optional sandbox-image pin. Must be a project-shared image; personal drafts are rejected — promote them first.

ProjectEnvironmentUpdateRequest.description: Only the fields you send change. `serverAttachmentId`, `skillSelection`, and `pluginVersionIds` are three-state: omit to leave unchanged, send `null` to CLEAR, send a value to set. An empty array is rejected — it is not a way to clear. Send at least one field besides `expectedRevision`. Unknown fields are rejected.

expectedRevision.description: The `revision` you last read. If the environment changed since, the write is rejected with 409 rather than clobbering the other edit.

description.description: Send an empty string to clear the description.

serverAttachmentId.description: `null` clears the pin and falls back to the host config's servers.

modelId.description: New model override, or `null` to CLEAR it and fall back to the host's model. Omit to leave unchanged. An empty string is rejected — it is not a way to clear.

secretSelection.description: `null` REVOKES the environment's credential grant; a value replaces it; omission leaves it unchanged. `[]` is rejected — an accidental empty array that read as "remove every credential" would break a workflow with no error to look at.

pluginVersionIds.description: Pinned plugin VERSION IDs. Narrow by design: the plugin must be installed and enabled, the version must be `ready`, at most one version per plugin may be pinned, and none of its skills may carry supporting files. Not a general-purpose plugin list. `null` clears all pins.

sandboxImageId.description: New sandbox-image pin, or null to clear it. Omit to leave unchanged.

ProjectEnvironmentRevisionRequest.description: The optimistic-concurrency precondition. Unknown fields are rejected.

expectedRevision.description: The `revision` you last read for this environment.

ProjectEnvironmentResolved.description: What an environment resolves to right now — the same resolution an eval run performs.

hostConfigId.description: The host's config at resolve time — hosts rotate configs live, so this can change without the environment's `revision` changing.

modelId.description: The environment's stored override, when it sets one.

effectiveModelId.description: The model this environment WILL RUN — the override if it has one, else the host config's. Always present on a successful resolve: an environment with no model anywhere cannot be resolved for launch and fails with 409 `details.reason: "environment_model_required"`.

sandboxImageId.description: The environment's sandbox-image pin, when set.

effectiveServerIds.description: `selectedServerIds` plus the servers contributed by pinned plugin versions — the set a run actually connects. Identical to `selectedServerIds` when no plugins are pinned.

pluginVersions.description: The resolved plugin version pins, in pin order.

servers.description: Connectable projection of `effectiveServerIds`, healed to the current live servers.

SandboxImageBlueprintValidateResult.description: Lint result. `ok: true` carries the resolved base digest; `ok: false` carries structured errors. Always returned with HTTP 200 — an invalid blueprint is a successful lint.

baseImageDigest.description: Resolved sha256 digest of `base` (present when ok).

path.description: Location of the violation, e.g. `initialize[0].run` (empty for document-level errors).

messages.description: The conversation so far, oldest first. The caller owns state and resends the full history each turn. Each message content is capped at 8,000 characters AND 8,192 UTF-8 bytes; the whole history is additionally capped at 98,304 UTF-8 bytes (96 KB).

content.description: Plain text. Max 8,000 characters and 8,192 UTF-8 bytes.

idempotencyKey.description: A STABLE identity for the triggering event — not a fresh uuid per attempt. Each write the turn performs derives its own key from this one, so a retried turn re-issues the same mutations onto the same rows instead of authoring duplicates. Printable ASCII only (the value becomes a header on every write the turn issues). Omitting it preserves the older non-idempotent behaviour rather than being rejected.

conversationId.description: Where an approval control can be rendered for this turn (a channel, a thread, a DM). Its presence is what makes the GATED tools available at all: without somewhere to collect a click, the turn is not offered them, so the model never proposes an action nobody can approve.

slackChannelId.description: Slack-named spelling of `conversationId`. Both are accepted indefinitely; `conversationId` wins when both are sent.

reply.description: The assistant's final text for this turn.

operation.description: Platform operation name invoked during the turn.

createdResources.description: Resources the turn created, with app deep links.

type.description: Resource type. New types may be added; render an unknown type generically rather than dropping it.

proposedActions.description: Actions the turn wants to take but may not take on its own — they SPEND, or reach a third-party system. Nothing here has happened: each entry is a persisted proposal awaiting a human click. The `actionId` is all an approval control needs to carry, because the server holds what the action does; the remaining fields are for RENDERING only and must never be echoed back as instructions.

actionId.description: Opaque id. The only value a click may carry.

operation.description: Platform operation name. Display and telemetry only.

description.description: Short summary of the TARGET, not a cost estimate. Model-influenced text — escape before rendering.

buttonLabel.description: Verb for the approval control, e.g. "Run it".

kind.description: What approving it does, so a host can word its confirmation and its after-the-fact announcement truthfully. Treat an unrecognised value as neutral rather than guessing.

confirmSeverity.description: How stern the confirmation copy should be: `spend` consumes quota or credits, `external` runs somewhere MCPJam does not control and cannot undo, `none` states explicitly that the default cost warning would be FALSE for this action (disabling a schedule stops spend). Absent means the host's default copy is honest enough.

type.description: Resource type the proposal is about, e.g. `eval_suite`.

selector.description: The validated input's own selector for it — an id where the server minted the proposal, possibly a name where the model authored it. Match against both.

target.description: What the proposal is about, for correlating it with other turn output (e.g. suppressing a duplicate run affordance on the created suite it already offers to run). Display/dedup only — never an instruction. Absent means match-unknown; fall back to coarser behavior.

EvalRunEnvironment.description: The project environment a run is pinned to, at the revision resolved when it launched. `null` for a legacy run that used the suite's saved server selection.

revision.description: The environment revision the run executed against.

ProjectCreateRequest.description: Neither a client config nor a server map is required: the backend seeds both. Requires membership of the target organization, and counts against the plan's project limit.

organizationId.description: Defaults to the caller's default organization when omitted.

ProjectUpdateRequest.description: Metadata only, and at least one field is required. The project's server map is deliberately NOT updatable here: the underlying mutation treats it as a wholesale replace and deletes every server absent from the payload. Use the per-server routes instead. Requires project admin.

ProjectServerCreateRequest.description: Creates a saved server in the project. Server names are unique per workspace — a clash responds `409`. Scope comes from the path: `projectId`, `serverId` and `workspaceId` are rejected in the body.

env.description: Stored encrypted; never returned by any read.

headers.description: Stored encrypted; never returned by any read.

clientSecret.description: Stored encrypted; never returned. Reads expose only `hasClientSecret`.

ProjectServerUpdateRequest.description: Sparse update — omitted fields are unchanged, and at least one field is required. Editing a server that is shared as an OAuth connection requires project admin.

env.description: Stored encrypted; never returned by any read.

headers.description: Stored encrypted; never returned by any read.

clientSecret.description: Stored encrypted; never returned. Reads expose only `hasClientSecret`.

clearClientSecret.description: Removes the stored client secret. Mutually exclusive with `clientSecret`.

ClientServersRequest.description: Replaces the client's server attachments wholesale. Every id must name a live server in the same project. Per-server connection overrides are trimmed to the surviving selection.

optionalServerIds.description: Attached but not required to connect.

expectedConfigId.description: The `configId` you last read for this client. ALWAYS required here: this operation rewrites the config, and without the token a write composed from a stale read silently reverts whatever landed in between. A mismatch is `409 CONFLICT` carrying `details.currentConfigId`.

expectedImpact.description: The `impact` you last read for this client. Optional, and checked transactionally when sent — a consumer added or removed since you read it makes the write conflict (`details.currentImpact`) instead of quietly affecting more than you were told it would.

ClientDuplicateRequest.description: Optional name for the copy; defaults to a derived name.

ServerConnection.description: The state of one "connect this MCP server" request. Every server-connection route returns this shape, so a caller polls exactly what it created.

connectionRequestId.description: Public `scr_…` identifier. Safe to print; it is never sufficient to act on a request.

handoffUrl.description: Where the user finishes in a browser, for both `awaiting_project` and `awaiting_authorization`. Returned ONLY by the create call — the raw token behind it is minted once and never stored. Treat it as a private, single-person capability: never post it to a shared channel.

url.description: Redacted: query values are replaced, because a keyed-endpoint URL's query can be the credential.

retryable.description: Whether retrying THIS request could succeed.

candidates.description: Present only on AMBIGUOUS_SERVER: the saved servers the URL matched, so the caller can re-send with a serverId.

url.description: The MCP server URL to connect.

projectId.description: Omit to have the user choose in the browser; a request with no project resolves to `awaiting_project` rather than defaulting to one.

serverId.description: Disambiguates when a project already has several saved servers on this URL.

name.description: Used only if a server row is created. Ignored when an existing row is reused.

reauthorize.description: Skip deduplication and force a fresh authorization.

modelOverrides.description: `modelId` is accepted on environment create and update.

modelMatrix.description: Environment cells may vary by model on one host (the compare grid).

ephemeralEnvironmentLaunch.description: `startTestSuiteRun` / the v1 group route accept `ephemeralEnvironment` — a project-scoped env may launch without suite membership. Absent or false on older backends.

Persona.description: A reusable synthetic character. The GOAL lives on the journey, not here — one persona can be pointed at many different tasks.

id.description: Durable id — what journeys reference and what every route here addresses.

slug.description: Stable slug key, shared with exported session data. Useful for correlating transcripts; NOT an address for this API.

source.description: How the persona came to exist.

seedKeywords.description: Present on cluster-derived personas: the terms the cluster was built from.

avatar.description: Look, as indices into the app's fixed shape/palette sets. `null` when unset — the app then derives one from the id.

nextCursor.description: Present only when another page exists. Opaque — do not parse it.

role.description: What this person is, in the product's terms — "finance ops lead", "first-time buyer". 1–120 characters.

notes.description: Free-text context the model is grounded in. Up to 2000 characters.

avatarShape.description: Index into the app's fixed shape set. Out of range is a 400 naming the field, not an upstream error about a constant you have never seen.

avatarPalette.description: Index into the app's fixed palette set.

PersonaUpdateRequest.description: At least one field is required — an empty patch is a 400 rather than a silent no-op.

role.description: What this person is, in the product's terms — "finance ops lead", "first-time buyer". 1–120 characters.

notes.description: Free-text context the model is grounded in. Up to 2000 characters.

avatarShape.description: Index into the app's fixed shape set. Out of range is a 400 naming the field, not an upstream error about a constant you have never seen.

avatarPalette.description: Index into the app's fixed palette set.

Journey.description: A persona's task: what they are trying to accomplish, and across which targets. Launching one is `POST /projects/{projectId}/journeys/{journeyId}/runs`.

goal.description: What the persona is trying to accomplish. This drives the whole run.

swarmId.description: The swarm container this journey was authored under. Provenance only — nothing resolves through it at run time, and a journey created outside a swarm has none.

environmentIds.description: Environments this journey fans out across. EMPTY on a host-pinned journey — that is a different execution model, not a journey with no targets.

serverAttachmentId.description: Legacy host-pinned grounding. Absent on an environment-based journey.

sessionsPerTarget.description: Sessions run against EACH target. Total sessions = targets × this.

nextCursor.description: Present only when another page exists. Opaque — do not parse it.

personaId.description: An existing persona in this project.

swarmId.description: Authoring provenance only — which swarm container this was made in.

environmentIds.description: The environments to fan out across. NON-EMPTY when present: `[]` reads as "these, naming none", and would silently fall back to something else.

JourneyUpdateRequest.description:
PATCH with a TRI-STATE, and the third state is the point: a field absent leaves it alone, present sets it, and `null` CLEARS it. There is no other way to say "stop fanning this journey out across environments and go back to its host targets".

`sessionsPerTarget` and `maxTurns` must be sent TOGETHER — they are one config object upstream, so a partial update would need a read-modify-write that could silently clobber a concurrent edit. Requiring both is a 400 you can fix rather than a lost update you never see.

environmentIds.description: A non-empty list to set, or `null` to clear and fall back to host targets.

JourneyArchived.description: Journeys ARCHIVE rather than delete: existing runs keep pointing at the definition they executed.

Swarm.description: An authoring container for journeys. It holds DEFAULTS, not execution state — launching happens per journey.

environmentIds.description: Default fan-out for journeys authored under this container.

nextCursor.description: Present only when another page exists. Opaque — do not parse it.

SwarmUpdateRequest.description: Same tri-state as the journey patch (`null` clears), and the same rule that `sessionsPerTarget` and `maxTurns` travel together.

PersonaGenerateRequest.description: Exactly ONE grounding source: `serverAttachmentId` or `environmentId`. Sending both is a 400 — a request that is already confused about what it wants should not have a winner picked for it.

personaCount.description: Ask for a SLATE of N personas. Omitting it is not the same as `1`: it selects the legacy single-persona response shape, so a default would switch the response under a caller that only knows the other one.

description.description: Free-text audience brief, forwarded verbatim into the prompt.

existingPersonas.description: Personas you already have, so the model drafts different ones. A prompt hint, not a data feed — only the first few dozen are used.

JourneyGenerateRequest.description: Exactly ONE grounding source: `serverAttachmentId` or `environmentId`. Sending both is a 400 — a request that is already confused about what it wants should not have a winner picked for it.

persona.description: The persona to draft journeys FOR, passed BY VALUE rather than by id. Not an oversight: the create flow drafts a persona and its journeys before either exists, so requiring a persisted persona would force you to save a draft you may discard.

GenerationDrafts.description:
DRAFTS. Nothing here is persisted — feed what you want to keep to `POST /projects/{projectId}/personas` or `POST /projects/{projectId}/journeys`.

The shape depends on the request: `POST /personas/generate` returns `{persona, journeys}` without `personaCount` and `{personas: [{persona, journeys}]}` with it; `POST /journeys/generate` returns `{journeys}`.

PersonaDraft.description: A generated persona draft. Nothing is persisted until you create it.

Secret.description: A project credential — METADATA ONLY, always. There is no `value` field on this schema and no route that returns one: a secret is written and delivered into a run, never read back.

name.description: The environment-variable name (`^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*$`). This IS the secret's identity: what a materialized delivery exports, what a workflow references, and what stays stable across a rotation. Immutable.

delivery.description: `brokered` — the sandbox's egress proxy injects the value as a request header OUTSIDE the VM, so the box never holds it. Prevents EXTRACTION, not USE: any process in the box can call the bound host while the policy is live, and it works for HTTPS APIs only (domain rules bind on ports 80/443). `materialized` — a real environment variable inside the box, which is the only thing a CLI can read; EXTRACTABLE BY DESIGN.

brokerHosts.description: Brokered only: the exact hostnames the header is injected on.

brokerTemplate.description: Brokered only: the header value, with `{}` where the secret goes.

sharing.description: `project` — admin-managed, delivered to every member's sessions. `user` — personal, delivered ONLY in sessions its owner starts and silently absent from anyone else's run of the same environment. Immutable.

ownerUserId.description: Personal secrets only. Project-shared rows have no owner.

lastDeliveredAt.description: When this secret was last HANDED TO a run — not when it was last used. Brokered use is unobservable by construction (the proxy injects the header; the request is never seen here), so `used` would be a number nobody can honestly produce. `null` means nothing has been recorded, which is not the same as never delivered.

nextCursor.description: Present only when another page exists. Opaque — do not parse it.

SecretCreateRequest.description: THE VALUE TRAVELS IN THIS BODY and becomes visible to whatever makes the call — its process, its logs, its shell history. Supply it from a file or an environment variable rather than pasting it into a command.

name.description: Environment-variable name. Immutable — renaming is delete-and-recreate.

value.description: The credential. Stored encrypted; no route ever returns it. NOT trimmed — a trailing newline is meaningful in a PEM block, and rewriting what you sent would present as 'the key is wrong' with nothing to look at.

delivery.description: Required, with no default: a caller who has not said whether the value ends up inside the sandbox has not made the decision this field exists for. See `Secret.delivery`.

brokerHosts.description: Required for `brokered`, forbidden for `materialized`. Exact hostnames — no scheme, no port, no wildcard: the proxy matches a host, and a URL installs a rule that silently never fires.

brokerTemplate.description: Required for `brokered`, forbidden for `materialized`. The header value with `{}` where the secret goes, e.g. `Bearer {}`. A template without `{}` is rejected: it installs a constant header that never carries the credential.

sharing.description: Defaults to `project`. A non-admin asking for it is refused rather than downgraded to personal — a silent downgrade looks like success and then reaches nobody else's sessions.

SecretUpdateRequest.description: At least one field. `name` and `sharing` are absent because both are IMMUTABLE: renaming would break the workflows referencing the environment variable, and re-sharing would change who has already been handed the value. Delete and recreate for either. A rotation reaches NEW RUNS ONLY — a session already running holds the old value and cannot be reached.

value.description: The new credential. Same exposure as on create: it travels in this body.

description.description: `null` clears it; omit to leave it unchanged.

delivery.description: Switching to `brokered` requires the host binding in the same call; switching to `materialized` clears it.

brokerHosts.description: Required for `brokered`, forbidden for `materialized`. Exact hostnames — no scheme, no port, no wildcard: the proxy matches a host, and a URL installs a rule that silently never fires.

brokerTemplate.description: Required for `brokered`, forbidden for `materialized`. The header value with `{}` where the secret goes, e.g. `Bearer {}`. A template without `{}` is rejected: it installs a constant header that never carries the credential.

SecretDeleted.description: A HARD delete: the row and the encrypted value both go. This is the revoke button, so it is not soft.

name.description: Echoed so a caller logging the revoke needs no prior read.

suggestedChecks.description: Deterministic checks the backend suggests. Only `toolCalledAtLeastOnce` is ever suggested — it is the one kind whose validity the grounding snapshot can prove, because the tool provably exists.

targetId.description: Execution identity. TWO TARGETS CAN SHARE A `hostId` — two environments may resolve to the same host with different servers — so this, not `hostId`, is what identifies a target within a run.

JourneyRunAttempt.description: One session's execution record: (target, session index).

chatSessionId.description: `null` until the attempt claims a session.

status.description: `pending` → `running` → terminal. A `pending` attempt cannot jump straight to a terminal state.

errorMessage.description: Capped and redacted before it reaches this response.

waveId.description: The batch this run was launched with. Sibling runs of one co-launched wave share it; a solo relaunch is a wave of one. Absent on a run launched without one.

status.description: Poll until it leaves `running`.

canceled.description: True when somebody STOPPED this run. **Check this before showing a run as a failure**: a cancelled run reports `status: "failed"`, because cancellation is recorded as a marker rather than a status of its own.

stale.description: True when the runner went silent and the watchdog settled the run. Distinct from a run that failed while still reporting.

persona.description: The persona AS PINNED AT LAUNCH, from the run's immutable snapshot — not the persona's current values, which may have been edited since.

attempts.description: Per-session execution records. Present on the single-run read only — lists stay compact.

targetSummaries.description: The same counts as `summary`, broken down per target.

lastHeartbeatAt.description: Epoch milliseconds of the runner's last check-in. A long-stale heartbeat on a `running` run is what the watchdog acts on.

insights.description: The common actionable-insights envelope. Present on the DETAIL response only — lists stay compact — and absent when the caller may not have it or the deployment cannot produce one. Treat absence exactly like `status: "not_available"`.

nextCursor.description: Present only when another page exists.

id.description: The session's document id — the same value `GET /chat-sessions` returns as `id`, so a session found here can be looked up there.

chatSessionId.description: The RUNTIME key for the same session, used by the chat transport and the app's deep links. Distinct from `id` and NOT interchangeable with it.

status.description: ARCHIVAL state. A run session stays `active` forever unless archived, so this says nothing about how the run went — read `outcome` for the verdict.

outcome.description: How this session's attempt ended. `null` when the attempt cannot be matched (historical runs); absent on servers that predate the field.

preview.description: First message only. The transcript is a separate read.

nextCursor.description: Present only when another page exists.

JourneyRunLaunchRequest.description: Optional. A launch with no options is a BODYLESS POST — omit the body entirely rather than sending `null`, which is rejected.

waveId.description: Opaque id linking the sibling runs of one co-launched batch. Mint it yourself and reuse it across the launches you want grouped.

environmentIds.description: Fan out across THESE environments instead of the journey's authored targets. NON-EMPTY when present: `[]` is a caller saying "across these" while naming none, and would have silently launched the authored targets instead. Silently running something other than what was asked for is bad anywhere; on an operation that spends it is worse. Omit the field to mean "as authored".

id.description: The run id. Poll it, or stop it with `cancel`.

status.description: Always `running` — the run row exists and its fan-out has started. This is a 202: nothing here says the journey has finished, only that it is under way.

deduped.description: True when an `Idempotency-Key` replayed onto a run that ALREADY existed, so nothing new was started. The response is otherwise identical, which is how a retry of a dropped request tells "I launched it" from "it was already going" without a second read.

status.description: The run's terminal status after the cancel settled it.

alreadyCanceled.description: True when the run was already cancelled and this call did nothing.

finalized.description: Attempts this call moved to terminal. Zero on an idempotent replay.

pendingCount.description: Claimed for grading and unfinished — includes crashed runners.

failedGradingCount.description: Sessions whose GRADING broke. Deliberately separate from `failCount`: folding them together makes a crashed judge look like a regression.

RunScorecard.description: Deterministic rubric result for one run. NO MODEL IS INVOLVED and nothing is spent — reach for this before the model-generated wave insights, which usually is not the question you actually have.

criteria.description: EVERY criterion the run's rubric declared, in snapshot order — including ones nothing was graded against. An absent row would be indistinguishable from a criterion that was never configured.

sessionsGraded.description: The DENOMINATOR for any rate you compute. Never divide by `sessionsTotal` — 3 failures of 4 graded sessions out of 40 attempted is not 7.5%.

SwarmFinding.description: A criterion that keeps failing, tracked ACROSS waves. One finding is one problem over time, not one row per occurrence.

fingerprint.description: Stable identity across waves — this is what makes a streak a streak rather than a new finding each time.

id.description: Identity. The fingerprint is built from this, never from the label.

label.description: Display only; refreshed on every firing so renames show through.

status.description: A LIFECYCLE: first seen, seen again, came back after being resolved, stopped firing. Note what is NOT here — `dismissed` is not a status. Dismissal is the orthogonal `dismissedAt` below, so a finding can be both recurring and dismissed.

dismissedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds. ORTHOGONAL to `status` — dismissing hides a finding from your view without claiming it stopped happening.

nextCursor.description: Present only when another page exists.

dismissed.description: The finding's dismissal state AFTER this call.

sessionsGraded.description: The DENOMINATOR for any rate you compute. Never divide by the session total.

runStreak.description: Consecutive runs of this journey where the criterion failed.

journeyArchived.description: The run stays readable after its journey is archived; this is how you tell.

goalCompletion.description: `null` when nothing has been graded — never zeroes, which would read as "everything failed".

SwarmOverview.description: Project-wide roll-up across recent runs. Deterministic; nothing is spent.

runsConsidered.description: How many runs the roll-up scanned. Bounded — this is not "all runs ever".

passRate.description: `null` when nothing is graded yet — never `0`, which would read as "everything failed".

WaveInsights.description: Model analysis over a whole wave. Produced asynchronously — POLL this rather than re-requesting, because a second request SPENDS again.

insights.description: The DIRECTED lane: an explanation of the findings the deterministic pass already surfaced. `null` until generation completes. An opaque object — read it, do not pattern-match its internals.

discovery.description: The DISCOVERY lane: what the model noticed unprompted. `null` while only the directed lane has finished, which is a normal intermediate state rather than a failure. Opaque, like `insights`.

force.description: Regenerate over a wave that already has insights. OFF by default because it SPENDS a second time against your organization's shared daily ledger — and the common cause of a repeated request is a caller that did not poll.

Scenario.description: A published environment: what a visitor lands on when you share a link.

mode.description:
Who may open the share link:
- `project_members` — signed-in members of the project only
- `invited_only` — named members, invited individually
- `anyone_with_link` — **anyone holding the URL**, signed in or not

accessVersion.description: Bumped whenever access NARROWS — a mode change, or a member removal. Sessions minted under an older version stop working, which is what makes those changes take effect at once rather than at expiry. A link ROTATION is deliberately not one of them: it mints a new URL without bumping this, so anyone who already redeemed the old link keeps working. Rotating is half of closing a leak — see the rotate-link operation.

link.description: The share link. `null` when the scenario has no link token.

created.description: False when the environment was ALREADY published and this returned the existing scenario. Publishing is idempotent, so this is how you tell "I published it" from "it was already there" without a preflight read.

overridesIgnored.description: True when the create-time overrides (`name`, `description`, `mode`) were NOT applied because the environment was already published. Paired with `created: false` — change an existing scenario with `PATCH .../user-testing/scenarios/{scenarioId}`.

ScenarioPublishRequest.description: Optional CREATE-TIME overrides, applied in the same call so the scenario is never briefly live in a wider mode than you asked for. Ignored on a republish — see `overridesIgnored`.

mode.description:
Who may open the share link:
- `project_members` — signed-in members of the project only
- `invited_only` — named members, invited individually
- `anyone_with_link` — **anyone holding the URL**, signed in or not

deleted.description: False when the environment had no scenario. NOT an error — unpublishing something already unpublished is a no-op.

UserTestingScenario.description: Scenario metadata after an update. Deliberately WITHOUT `accessVersion`: a mode change bumps it upstream, but the envelope this route re-reads does not carry the new value — reporting a stale one would document a revocation signal the response cannot deliver. The publish response carries the real one.

ScenarioUpdateRequest.description: At least one field. **Send `mode` on its own**: identity and exposure are separate operations upstream, and applying them in sequence could leave the scenario live in a mode you did not ask for.

mode.description:
Who may open the share link:
- `project_members` — signed-in members of the project only
- `invited_only` — named members, invited individually
- `anyone_with_link` — **anyone holding the URL**, signed in or not

UserTestingSession.description: One visitor's session with a published scenario. A SUMMARY, not a transcript.

id.description: The address for the transcript route.

preview.description: First message only. The transcript is a separate, explicit read.

authInterrupted.description: The visitor abandoned mid-flow because a server demanded auth.

nextCursor.description: Present only when another page exists.

TranscriptMessage.description: One projected transcript message. Tool payloads and blobs are dropped.

UserTestingSessionDetail.description: A session's transcript, paged. The stored blob URL is NEVER returned: it is a direct handle with no further authorization, so handing it out would turn one authorized read into an unbounded, unrevocable one.

messageCount.description: `null` — never `0` — when the transcript could not be read. Zero would be a claim the visitor said nothing, the opposite of what an unreadable blob means, and a caller checking only this field would act on it.

transcriptUnavailable.description: True when the stored conversation could not be read. Distinct from an empty `messages`, which means the visitor genuinely said nothing.

GuestExecution.description: The spend dial for ANONYMOUS visitors. Replaced as a whole, never patched: these caps only mean something as a set, and a partial update that raised `dailyCreditCap` while leaving a stale `maxConcurrentComputers` behind would produce a combination nobody chose.

enabled.description: Master switch. Everything below is inert while this is false.

dailyCreditCap.description: Hard ceiling on what visitors can spend per day, in credits.

link.description: The NEW share link. The old one stops working immediately.

removed.description: The id or email that was removed, echoed back.

ScenarioMemberRequest.description: UPSERT by email, so re-inviting somebody is not an error.

sendInviteEmail.description: OFF by default: adding somebody quietly is not the same as inviting them.

environmentId.description: The environment to point this scenario at. Must belong to the SAME project.

ActionableFindingEvidence.description: One citation behind a finding. Evidence is what makes a finding checkable rather than an assertion.

excerpt.description: Scrubbed and clipped at the producer. Never a full transcript.

ActionableFinding.description: One actionable finding. The fields are ordered from cheapest to trust to most: `observed` is deterministic, `recommendation` is the model's, and `evidence` lets you check both.

id.description: Stable remediation id (`rf_<16 hex>`). Survives dynamic error values, so the same problem keeps the same id across runs — dismiss it once and it stays dismissed.

signalFingerprint.description: The registry signal this derives from. Several findings can share one.

attribution.description: WHOSE problem this is. `server_*` points at the MCP server; `agent_or_prompt` and `test_design` point back at the caller.

actionTarget.description: What you would change to fix it.

actionability.description: `ready` means the finding names a specific target and change. `investigate` means it does not yet. `informational` means there is nothing to do.

observed.description: DETERMINISTIC observation — counts and identities, never model prose. This is the part you can verify yourself.

acceptanceCriteria.description: How you would know the fix worked.

affected.description: How much of the analyzed population hit this. Read it as a ratio — `1/40` and `38/40` are different problems.

target.description: Present only when a server (and, for tool surfaces, a tool) resolved against the pinned snapshot. Required for `mcp_server` / `ready`.

snapshotHash.description: The pinned snapshot the target resolved against, so a finding cannot silently re-point at a definition that changed after it was written.

InsightScope.description: What this envelope is about. The extra fields depend on `kind`.

InsightsEnvelope.description:
The common insights envelope, shared by eval runs, swarm waves and user-testing windows.

One shape for three producers, so a caller writes the reading code once. An ABSENT envelope and `status: "not_available"` mean the same thing and both are normal: the field is an enrichment, and a caller who may not have it gets the resource without it rather than an error.

status.description: `not_available` means this deployment cannot produce insights at all — treat an ABSENT envelope the same way. `not_requested` means nobody has asked. `pending` means one is running: poll, do not re-request.

retryable.description: Whether asking again could produce a different answer. False on a `failed` envelope means the input, not the attempt, was the problem.

coverage.description: READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING ANY FINDING. `truncated` and `lowConfidence` are the difference between "this happens" and "this happened in the part we looked at".

truncated.description: The analysis saw `analyzed` of `total`, not all of it.

lowConfidence.description: Too little was analyzed to generalize. Findings still stand as observations of what WAS seen.

runHealth.description: Swarm only. Launch outcomes never appear as findings — a run that could not start is an operational fact, not something the server under test did.

truncation.description: What this RESPONSE dropped to stay a sane size, as distinct from what the ANALYSIS did not look at (`coverage`).

UserTestingScenarioDetail.description: A published scenario, enriched with findings over its latest analyzed window. NO `accessVersion`: the settings envelope this is read from does not carry it — the publish and rebind responses do.

insights.description: Present when the caller may have it. The envelope needs workspace MEMBERSHIP while the scenario itself is visible more widely, so a lower-privilege viewer gets the scenario without this field rather than a 403.

ScenarioMetrics.description:
Session metrics for the scenario: volumes, completion and feedback rates, cohort splits.

Deliberately UNPINNED. The upstream projection grows with the product and the SDK types it as an open record for the same reason — pinning a field list here would turn every added metric into a spec violation. Read what you recognize and ignore the rest.

ScenarioUsage.description:
Usage breakdown: models, tools and servers the scenario's sessions actually used.

**Read `scan.truncated` before quoting any rate from this.** True means the rates were computed over the most recent N sessions rather than all of them, and dropping the flag turns a conditional statistic into an unconditional claim.

Unpinned for the same reason as `ScenarioMetrics`.

ScenarioSignals.description:
What the miner extracted from the scenario's current window — and how you learn the current window id, which the window-insights read takes. There is no separate "list windows" route because the only window anyone asks about is the live one.

Unpinned; see `ScenarioMetrics`.

ScenarioWindowInsights.description: One window's generated insights, plus the `windowId` they belong to. The generated part is unpinned; see `ScenarioMetrics`.

ScenarioFinding.description: One finding over a scenario window. Unpinned; see `ScenarioMetrics`. The stable fields are the document id (used by dismiss/undismiss) and the dismissal state.

ScenarioInsightsRequest.description: Optional. A bodyless POST is the ordinary case.

force.description: Regenerate even when a completed generation already exists. SPENDS A SECOND TIME — that is the whole point of the flag, so it is never inferred.

windowId.description: The window this generation covers. Poll `GET .../windows/{windowId}/insights` with it.

ScenarioInsightsCancelRequest.description: Which generation to cancel. In the body rather than the path because the recovery case this exists for — a window stuck `pending` — is precisely when you have the id and nothing else works.

dismissed.description: True from `/dismiss`, false from `/undismiss`. Dismissal is keyed on the finding's stable remediation id, so the same problem stays dismissed across regenerations.

EvalRunInsightsRequest.description: Optional. A bodyless POST is the ordinary case.

force.description: Regenerate even when insights already exist. SPENDS AGAIN. Must be a real boolean — `"false"` is rejected rather than read as consent.

ProjectCapabilities.description:
What the caller may do in this project, asked BEFORE they try it.

**A planning aid, not a gate.** Every enforcement point is unchanged: the write path checks roles and the beta flag inside the platform regardless of what this returned a second earlier. A caller that reads a `true` here and races a flag flip gets the same clean `403` it would have got without asking. Nothing may consult this INSTEAD of its own check.

It exists because every agent surface MCPJam ships is static — one MCP tool catalog built with no organization in hand, a CLI command tree fixed at install — so an agent planning a task otherwise has to attempt the write and read the failure. By then it has usually already told a human what it was about to do.

role.description: The caller's ORGANIZATION role: `guest`, `member`, `admin` or `owner`. This is what the platform's role checks rank; a project grant does not raise it.

projectRole.description: `admin` or `editor`, when the caller holds a project grant.

surface.description: Which channel we resolved this request to arrive on. Echoed so an agent can confirm it is labelled the way it expects — a CLI showing up as `rest` means its user agent is not reaching us.

mode.description: `off` | `dark` | `enforce`. Only `enforce` turns a disabled flag into a refusal; in `dark` the platform logs what it would have blocked and lets the write through.

can.description: The booleans to branch on, derived server-side rather than left for each caller to re-derive from `role` plus flag state.

cancelJourneyRun.description: Stays TRUE for an organization that has lost the beta. Losing the feature is exactly when stopping a run matters most.

publishUserTestingScenario.description: Project admin, and behind the beta gate.

unpublishUserTestingScenario.description: Project admin, NOT gated — same reasoning as cancelling a run.

changeUserTestingExposure.description: Mode changes, member invites and removals, link rotation, renames — the controls an ordinary MEMBER can use, none of them gated. Guest execution is not covered here; it needs admin and has its own key.

manageUserTestingGuestExecution.description: The guest-execution spend caps. Project admin, ungated.

readEvals.description: Reading eval suites, runs, iterations and traces.

writeEvalSuites.description: Authoring suites and cases — every eval write short of deleting. Unlike the swarm keys this counts a project GRANT, not organization rank alone.

launchEvalRun.description: Starting a suite or case run.

deleteAnyEvalSuite.description: Deleting a suite SOMEONE ELSE created — the project admin tier. The creator of a suite may always delete it whatever their role, so `false` here does not mean you cannot delete your own.

deleteAnyEvalRun.description: Same tier and same creator exception, for runs.

exportEvalTraces.description: Whether the trace export surface is open. Export still filters row by row against the caller, so this does not promise every session in the project lands in the file.

ReadinessLaneCoverage.description: What one lane managed to look at, reported separately from what it found. A lane with zero violations and zero evaluated checks is not a pass, and publishing the denominator is the only way to keep those apart.

lane.description: Anthropic defines five lanes and OpenAI seven, overlapping on four. Which subset applies is decided by the run's `readinessKind`.

evaluated.description: Findings that reached a satisfied or violated verdict.

notEvaluated.description: Applicable but never exercised. Each one is an unanswered question.

notApplicable.description: Could not apply to this target; not a gap.

missingInputs.description: Named inputs the caller could supply to close the gap, for example `toolListing`. Empty when the gap is not the caller's to close.

ReadinessStageResult.description: One staged rollup. OpenAI grades a quick technical preflight and a full submission-ready verdict from the same findings; Claude has one rollup, already reported as `overallStatus`.

lanes.description: The lanes this stage rolled up, so the verdict is reproducible by hand.

ReadinessObservationState.description: The model-observation axis, independent of the run's own status. A run whose lanes graded cleanly is `completed` even when the observation call was refused for credit: a payment problem belongs to the account, never to the server under grading.

reason.description: Machine-readable, so a client branches rather than string-matching. `billing_limit_reached` is the value to key a top-up prompt on.

detail.description: A sentence for a human. Never parse it; branch on `reason`.

ReadinessRun.description: A directory-readiness run. Readiness carries no numeric score and is excluded from `pooledConformanceScore`: it answers whether a publisher would list this server, which is a different question from whether the server speaks MCP correctly.

serverId.description: The saved project server this run graded. Null only on rows written before the field existed.

serverUrl.description: The saved server's URL exactly as stored. Canonicalizing it would change the grade.

submissionMode.description: The declared submission shape, for an OpenAI run. Never inferred.

status.description: `cancelled` is distinct from `failed`: a person who stopped a run has learned nothing about their server.

overallStatus.description: The headline verdict. `incomplete` means nothing was violated and something the run needed was never evaluated.

capabilities.description: What the executing surface could actually do. Two surfaces grading one target agree only on their shared capability subset.

policySnapshotDate.description: The publisher-documentation snapshot this run graded against, so a stale grade says so.

includeLlmObservations.description: Whether this run was started with the paid observation opt-in.

ReadinessRunReceipt.description: The 202 receipt. Poll the run detail; do not re-POST.

status.description: The run's status when the start returned. `pending` for a fresh start; for a deduped start, whatever the existing run is already at — which may be `completed`, because a replayed idempotency key can name a run that finished long ago.

deduped.description: This request replayed an existing run rather than starting one.

ConformanceIngestRequest.description: Forwarded VERBATIM to the backend's conformance-ingestion surface, which owns the schema. The `projectId` path segment always wins.

ConformanceIngestResponse.description: The backend's response, passed through verbatim along with its status code. Success shapes are `{ ok: true, ... }` envelopes the SDK reporter parses. Errors are canonical v1 `{ code, message }`.

CatalogServer.description: Allowlisted projection of a scraped directory row. Extra upstream fields are dropped.

nextCursor.description: Opaque, filter-bound. Omitted on the last page.
Opaque, filter-bound. Omitted on the last page.
Opaque, filter-bound. Omitted on the last page.
Opaque, filter-bound. Omitted on the last page.

idempotencyKey.description: STABLE identity for this turn's intent — reuse it when retrying. A fresh key per attempt deduplicates nothing and will bill the turn twice. Printable ASCII only.

message.description: The message to send, as the user.

projectId.description: Required to START a session; ignored when continuing one.

sessionId.description: Continue this session. Omit to start a new one.

modelId.description: Provider-prefixed model id, e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`. Required on a first turn. A BARE id is rejected with `details.reason: "MODEL_AMBIGUOUS"` rather than guessed — an unprefixed id is indistinguishable from a local Ollama model, and guessing would spend on the wrong rail.

environmentId.description: Target this environment's servers. Mutually exclusive with `serverIds`. First turn only.

serverIds.description: Target these project servers. Mutually exclusive with `environmentId`. First turn only. Server CONFIGS are never accepted — only ids the project already holds.

temperature.description: First turn only — pinned to the session and reused on every continuation.

toolMode.description: `read_only` advertises only tools annotated `readOnlyHint: true`. `auto` advertises everything and MAY CAUSE REAL EXTERNAL SIDE EFFECTS. First turn only.

allowedServerIds.description: Narrow THIS TURN to a subset of the target's servers. An empty array narrows to none and is rejected — omit the field to use the whole target. Per-turn, not pinned.

allowedTools.description: Advertise only these tool names, for THIS TURN. An empty array advertises no tools at all — the same request as `maxToolCalls: 0`. Per-turn, not pinned.

maxToolCalls.description: Cap the tool calls this turn may make, enforced at DISPATCH rather than by bounding steps (one step can emit several parallel calls). `0` advertises no tools at all.

input.description: The raw arguments sent, scrubbed of protocol annotations (`_meta`, `$`-prefixed keys) and bounded.

output.description: The raw result, scrubbed and bounded. Absent when no result was recorded.

truncated.description: The payload was clipped. Always announced — a silently shortened result an agent believes is complete sends it debugging the wrong thing.

sessionId.description: The one public session id. Pass it back to continue, and to the trace/detail reads. NULL only when the turn ran but its transcript did not persist — which `persisted.outcome` reports, and which must not be read as "nothing happened": the turn already spent.

turnId.description: Minted by the turn lease and used by the ingest dedupe, so it names the same turn in both.

projectId.description: The project this turn ran in. On a continuation the caller never sent it — it comes off the session row — so this is the only place the response names the session's project.

advertisedToolCount.description: Tools the model could see this turn.

replay.description: Set when this idempotencyKey replayed an already-completed turn. Nothing was spent.

index.description: ABSOLUTE position in the stored transcript — the number trace spans reference. Never renumbered per page.

messageCount.description: NULL — never 0 — when the transcript could not be read. Zero would claim the conversation is empty.

spans.description: Same span shape as the eval iteration trace.

spansUnavailable.description: The spans could not be read. DISTINCT from an empty `spans` array, which means the turn genuinely made no recorded calls.

spansTruncated.description: Fewer spans came back than the turn recorded.

turnCount.description: Turns the session has in total, so a caller can tell whether the window is the whole story.

ambiguous.description: More than one element matched this role and name.

tree.description: Playwright ARIA snapshot of the widget frame.

elements.description: Interactive elements, in the same role/name/testId vocabulary the interaction steps accept.

truncated.description: The tree hit the character ceiling and was clipped.

note.description: Why nothing was captured, when nothing was.

status.description: The render verdict, e.g. `rendered`.

blockedRequests.description: Requests the render sandbox refused. A widget that renders while every fetch is blocked photographs perfectly and is broken, so this is reported even on a success.

screenshot.description: Present only when `includeScreenshot` was explicitly requested.

toolName.description: The MCP App tool to render. A tool that declares no `ui://` UI resource is refused (422) rather than run.

includeSnapshot.description: Return the widget as an accessibility tree with addressable elements. **Default true** — the reverse of the local Inspector route, because this endpoint's caller is usually a model for which a base64 image is the most expensive way to say nothing.

includeScreenshot.description: Also return a base64 image. **Default false**: it is by far the largest field this returns.

injectOpenAiCompat.description: Mount with the OpenAI Apps compatibility shims instead of the spec-default MCP-UI bridge.

GateWaiver.description: An audited, time-boxed override of an eval run's release gate. A waiver never changes the run's own `result` — the run keeps its verdict and every surface that honors the waiver says so out loud, which is what makes "no silent waiver" checkable rather than promised.

runId.description: The run this waiver covers. Suite-wide waivers are not honored.

reason.description: Why the gate was overridden, as the granter wrote it. Stored UNREDACTED and readable by anyone who can see the suite, for as long as the suite exists — never put secrets, tokens, or customer data in it.

expiresAt.description: Epoch ms. Always in the future when granted, and capped at 30 days out — there is no permanent waiver.

createdByEmail.description: `null`, never absent, when it cannot be resolved — a deleted user must not make a waiver look authorless.

active.description: Whether it is in force right now — neither revoked nor expired. Computed at read time; a client that must not honor a lapsed waiver should re-derive it from `expiresAt` rather than trust it.

policySnapshot.description: WHAT was overridden, captured at waive time so a later edit to the suite cannot rewrite the record. `null` for a run decided by the v2 verdict policy, whose identity is recorded on the audit event instead — this shape cannot hold it, and filling it in would be a false record rather than an incomplete one.

GateWaiverRead.description: The waiver in force over a run, or `null` when there is none.

GateWaiverWriteResult.description: The result of granting or revoking a waiver. `conflict` and `already_revoked` are IDEMPOTENT no-op successes, not failures.

status.description: `conflict` — a waiver was already in force, and `waiver` is that EXISTING one rather than a second row. `already_revoked` — this waiver had already been revoked, and `waiver` reports the original revocation rather than restamping it, so the record of who actually ended it survives a second call.

republishedChecks.description: GitHub Check Runs brought back in line by this write. A published check is a persisted verdict, not a live read, so `0` on a repository with checks connected means the status that gates the merge did not move.

EvalRunDecisionCounts.description: A tally WITH the population it counted. `measurementUnit` is never omitted and never inferred: under verdict policy v2 the counts are case-execution VARIANTS (repetitions are trials inside one, not members of it), and on a legacy run they are trials. A 3-case suite with 5 repetitions is legitimately 3 under one unit and 15 under the other, so a count reported without its unit is not a fact. On a `caseVariant` count every field is present and the three buckets sum to `total`; on a `trial` count each field is present only if the legacy run recorded it — absence stays absence rather than defaulting to zero.
